row.evidence: Highspot's pricing page lists three Contact-sales packages and names 'automated provisioning for large-scale deployments' as an enterprise capability, but its help centre and developer docs require sign-in, so SCIM itself is not publicly documented.
row.notes: Quote-only: Good (Equip and engage), Better (Train and practice) and Best (Coach and reinforce) are all Contact sales; enterprise capabilities (including APIs and 'automated provisioning for large-scale deployments') are sold on top. Highspot is now part of Seismic ('Highspot by Seismic'). The help centre (help.highspot.com), developer site (developers.highspot.com redirects to app sign-in) and API docs (api.highspot.com/v1.0/doc returns 401) all require sign-in, so SCIM, SSO plan and user-API details could not be verified; the Okta Integration Network has no Highspot app. If the gated docs confirm SCIM, this would be gated (quote-only, rule 6a).

plans.name: Coach and reinforce (Best)
plans.notes: Lists MCP Server and Insights Layer APIs.

plans.name: Enterprise capabilities (add-on)
plans.notes: Platform scale and extensibility: APIs, Data Lake access, multi-CRM support and 'automated provisioning for large-scale deployments'; not stated to be SCIM.

scim.notes: The pricing page mentions automated provisioning as an enterprise capability (c1) but no public page documents a SCIM endpoint; help centre and developer docs require sign-in.

audit_log_api.notes: Security page lists 'Real-time audit API integrations'; plan and scope not stated.

user_api.notes: APIs are named on the pricing page (Insights Layer APIs on Best; APIs under enterprise capabilities) and the security page mentions real-time audit API integrations, but the API reference (api.highspot.com/v1.0/doc, developers.highspot.com) requires sign-in, so no endpoints are recorded.

okta.notes: OIN search returns no results; /integrations/highspot/ is 404.

fallbacks.notes: Help centre, developer portal and API docs all require sign-in (help.highspot.com redirects to /hc/restricted).
